rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No repo/maintainer vocabulary (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood) appears in body prose above the maintainer cut.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 3 "It answers in essays": line 23: "**Never let the agent say everything.**" bolds a complete six-word imperative sentence (subject+verb+object), not a short handle sub-span. Rule text: "Bold the handle (≲ 5 words, a sub-span), never a whole lead sentence." Contrast with this same file's compliant handles — **sycophancy** (line 8) and **error cascade** (line 15) — each a single/two-word coined noun embedded inside a longer sentence, not a sentence unto itself. The maintainer block (line 36) labels this a "Handle... bolded at naming moment," but its shape (a full bolded directive clause) matches the pre-2026-07-09 whole-lead-sentence pattern rule 9 exists to end, not a coined-term handle; rule 9 carries no maintainer-attestation carve-out (unlike rule 7).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Shrink the bold to a short sub-span (e.g. bold only "say everything") or drop the bold and let the sentence read as plain mechanism prose.
